primaryQuestion: Does the bounded authorization-domain method improve task decisions, evidence support, and coverage honesty on the fixed real cases compared with an information-equivalent organized instruction?

questions.hypothesis: Compared with B, D reduces sink-local false positives, unsupported deployment inference, and false completeness while preserving detection of the source-visible process_file failure.

arms.name: information-equivalent organized instruction
arms.input: The same natural task, normative policy, allowed source files, conclusion enum, and required evidence/scope rules expressed in organized Markdown.
arms.support: Common read-only host isolation, answer contract, capture, and evaluator; no authorization-domain declaration expander or obligation/evidence-state helper.

arms.name: domain declaration plus bounded execution support
arms.input: The same task facts expressed as the minimal authorization declaration selected after T9.
arms.support: Deterministic normalization, declared-obligation expansion, bounded task rendering, evidence-reference checks, separate discovery/evidence states, and complete-claim rules.

questions.attribution: This is intentionally a whole-method comparison. D changes both representation and domain-specific support; any effect belongs to the intervention bundle, not to syntax alone.
controls: same exact allowed input files and repository ref
same policy facts, answer information, and case ordering policy
same fixed-context read-only capability in the first feasibility run
same output contract, host capture, timeout, and semantic evaluator
same repair policy; format recovery and any domain repair are separately counted
no internet, target-network access, project execution, or oracle visibility

questions.reasonDeferred: No evidence yet shows that a second author-facing syntax, rather than the domain helper and evaluation protocol, changes task quality or authoring burden. Adding M now would increase construction work without a distinct first-prototype decision.
questions.conditionalHypothesis: If later authoring traces show omitted relations or stale refs, a structured declaration may reduce first-draft omissions and correction effort when the same natural requirement is created and then changed to add an explicit write-grantee relation and a new source ref.

arms: organized Markdown authored from the same natural requirement
structured declaration authored from the same natural requirement
mustHoldConstant: same author model/person and starting context
same canonical helper, validation, repair opportunities, task facts, and target behavior
same change request and evaluation oracle
measures: author tokens, calls, elapsed time, and actual/unknown cost
futureComparison.reportingLimit: If the author is a model, label the result model-assisted authoring and do not report human minutes or human labor savings.

questions.includedInFirstPrototype: only if implementation exposes more than one input adapter
questions.hypothesis: Semantically equivalent supported inputs normalize to the same canonical declaration, rendered task, obligation IDs, validation decisions, and complete-claim behavior.
questions.method: deterministic unit tests with no model call
questions.decision: A mismatch is an implementation defect. Equivalence may retire a redundant adapter or syntax, but neither result establishes or refutes whole-method task value.
questions.scopeGuard: Do not build YAML, a second DSL syntax, or a second adapter solely to create a parity experiment.

feasibilityPanel.countingLimit: The panel is one project/ref with three real conditions and two designed variations. It can establish pipeline and method feasibility signals, not prevalence, cross-project generalization, or statistical significance.
feasibilityPanel.repetition: Run one matched B/D pair per real case for initial feasibility. Add predeclared repeats only if the next question is run-to-run stability; do not repeat merely to consume time or search for a favorable result.

metrics.primary: taskDecisionCorrect per real case, with no full success unless oracle-critical trace facts are present
qualityRequirements: source-visible failure detected without confusing file ownership and destination authorization
upstream-control case refuted without a sink-local false positive
deployment case abstains with conditional trace and decisive missing facts
completeness claim is bounded to declared/discovered scope
hidden omission is not silently erased
costAndOperation: generation, structured fallback, format repair, domain repair, and tool call counts separately
input, cached-input, output, and total observed tokens
actual USD where provider data exists and unknown USD separately
metrics.tradeoffRule: Do not require every metric to improve. Report quality gains with token/time/call costs and negative quality with any cost savings rather than collapsing them into one score.

interpretations.condition: D improves one or more predeclared task-quality failures while meeting all case-specific quality requirements and introduces no new critical error.
interpretations.decisionEffect: Proceed to a bounded cross-project or discovery-capability experiment; do not yet claim general effectiveness.

interpretations.condition: D improves evidence/coverage honesty or decisions but costs more tokens, calls, or time, or improves some cases while regressing another non-critical dimension.
interpretations.decisionEffect: Keep only the support responsible for the material quality gain if its measured cost is acceptable for the task; otherwise simplify and rerun the affected comparison.

interpretations.condition: B and D produce equally correct, adequately evidenced, scoped results on this panel.
interpretations.decisionEffect: Do not attribute value to D. Prefer the simpler organized instruction for this panel or choose a predeclared harder coverage/discovery question; do not infer the whole method is universally useless.

interpretations.condition: D adds false positives/negatives, unsupported claims, excessive abstention, or cost without a predeclared quality gain.
interpretations.decisionEffect: Revise or stop the bounded method; do not add syntax, adapters, or cases merely to rescue the result.

interpretations.condition: information, model/settings, source inputs, repair opportunities, oracle applicability, or runtime capability were unequal or failed in a way that prevents the intended comparison.
interpretations.decisionEffect: Fix the protocol defect and rerun only the affected matched unit; keep the result inconclusive rather than recoding it as support or negative.

historicalRevision.oldProposal: E9 proposed a 3-5 engineer-day C/P parity probe followed by a 2-4 engineer-day paired run.
historicalRevision.revision: Parity is now only a deterministic consistency check and no second representation is required. The first implemented slice should build one canonical declaration/helper path and compare whole-method B/D task behavior; implementation effort will be re-estimated from T7-T9 concrete module/tests rather than carrying forward unmeasured engineer-day numbers.
historicalRevision.stopRule: Equivalent adapters may retire a redundant representation; this does not stop the domain method. Whole-method decisions follow task-quality and cost evidence, not representation parity.
